## INSTALLING LIBRARIES

```{r}
library(rvest)
library(jsonlite)


```

## READING HTML / JSON FILES

```{r}

html_page <- read_html("Books.html")
html_table <- html_element(html_page, "table")

## TURN THE TABLES INTO R DATAFRAME

books_from_html <- html_table(html_table)

books_from_html

## READING THE JSON FILE

books_from_json <- fromJSON("Books.json")

books_from_json

## MAKING BOTH RESULTS AS DATAFRAME

books_from_html <- as.data.frame(books_from_html)
books_from_json <- as.data.frame(books_from_json)


## MAKING EVERY COLUMN AS TEXT IN BOTH DATAFRAMES

books_from_html[] <- lapply(books_from_html, as.character)
books_from_json[] <- lapply(books_from_json, as.character)

print(books_from_html)
print(books_from_json)

## COMPARING THE TWO DATAFRAMES

identical(books_from_html, books_from_json)

names(books_from_html)
names(books_from_json)

## after comparing i observed that the html file has the column headers in uppercase while the json file has it in lowercase and since i prefer uppercase i am going to convert the json to uppercase 


```

## MAKING BOTH DATAFRAMES UPPERCASE

```{r}
names(books_from_html) <- toupper(names(books_from_html))
names(books_from_json) <- toupper(names(books_from_json)) 

```

## COMPARING THE DATAFAMES - CONFIRMATION

```{r}
identical(books_from_html, books_from_json)

names(books_from_html)
names(books_from_json)
```

## CONCLUSION AND FINDINGS

In this assignment, I created HTML and JSON files containing information about three real estate books. I used R to read the information from each file into a data frame. At first, the column headings were formatted differently: the HTML headings began with capital letters, while the JSON headings were lowercase. I changed the headings to a consistent format so R could compare the data correctly. I also made the book titles uppercase in both data frames.

After these changes, I compared the two data frames to check whether they contained the same information. This assignment helped me understand how HTML tables and JSON files organize data, and how R can read and compare information stored in different formats.
